analysis:
The supplied changes are documentation only: docs/architecture/inference.md and docs/reference/configuration.md. The patch excerpt of inference.md is truncated, and the visible head units (lines 1658-2251) show unchanged surrounding text. The changed ranges at 1493-1505 and 1553-1586 are not visible as numbered text. That includes the new 'Streamed auto tool calls' section, which is only partially visible in the patch excerpt.

The docs describe two new default-on env switches in docs/reference/configuration.md lines 415-416: DARKBLOOM_TTFT_STREAM_TOOL_CALLS and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_THINK_CONTENT_SEED.
- Streamed auto tool calls: for tool_choice auto on Gemma/Qwen35/Harmony/JSON formats, the provider now emits name and argument fragments incrementally before the frame closes. The docs say each call is still validated at frame close. This could affect T-008 and T-010 if streaming fragments were emitted outside the encryption path, or if cancellation or validation failures leave already-sent partial calls. A consumer would then receive tool-call fragments that later fail validation. Streaming goes through MLXOpenAIService.streamChatCompletionFrames, which the docs say is encrypted and sent over the coordinator connection, so the T-008 fail-closed encryption behavior is presumably preserved. That is unverified because the code is not supplied.
- Think-content seed: Qwen streams start in content state when no think marker is present. This is a parsing-state change, not a security boundary change. The risk is leaking reasoning text as content if the model emits reasoning without a tag. That is an output-quality issue, not a threat-model asset exposure, since the content already belongs to the consumer.

No changes were made to attestation, keys, App Attest, the cache, or the fan helper. No source code was supplied, so the actual implementation (ToolStreamPreparation.swift, ReasoningPromptProbe.swift) needs review in the code PR. The docs alone do not establish a regression.
